Which proposed test case should NOT be part of the ATDD test cases?
options: Mute a player from the scoreboard and check you no longer hear them
Check that a muted player is automatically reported to the moderators
After muting, check that your teammates still hear the muted player
Mute a player in round 1 and check they are still muted in round 3
why: ATDD test cases must cover the story and must not go beyond it. Automatic reporting is in neither the story nor its criteria.

distractorNotes.A: Covers the first criterion (positive test).
distractorNotes.C: Covers the third criterion: muting affects only the player who mutes.
distractorNotes.D: Covers the second criterion: muted for the rest of the match.

stem: Story: "As a player, I want a countdown before a match starts, so that I can get ready." Acceptance criteria: the countdown runs from 5 to 1; player input is ignored during the countdown; practice mode has no countdown. Tests: T1 start a ranked match and see 5 to 1; T2 start a casual match and see 5 to 1; T3 press fire during the countdown and check nothing happens; T4 start practice mode and check there is no countdown. Which pair of test cases should be reduced to one?
options: T1 and T3
T1 and T2
T3 and T4
T2 and T4
why: No two ATDD test cases should describe the same characteristic. T1 and T2 both check the 5-to-1 countdown; the criteria make no difference between ranked and casual matches.

distractorNotes.A: T1 checks the countdown and T3 the ignored input: two different criteria.
distractorNotes.C: T3 checks ignored input and T4 practice mode: two different criteria.
distractorNotes.D: T2 checks the countdown and T4 its absence in practice mode: two different criteria.

stem: At the start of ATDD for a crafting story, the designer, a developer and the tester discuss the story and notice it does not say what happens when the inventory is full. They agree on the behaviour and add an acceptance criterion. Which part of ATDD is this?
options: Creating the test cases
The specification workshop
Executing the acceptance tests
Automating the tests as executable requirements
why: In the specification workshop the team analyses, discusses and writes the story and its acceptance criteria, resolving incompleteness and ambiguities.

distractorNotes.A: Test cases are created after the workshop, from the agreed criteria.
distractorNotes.C: Nothing is executed yet; the story is still being clarified.
distractorNotes.D: Automation comes when the test cases exist and the feature is being implemented.

stem: Acceptance criterion: "Given a player with 100 gems, when they buy a 30-gem emote, then their balance is 70 gems and the emote is in their collection." Which test case is derived correctly from it?
options: Precondition: 100 gems. Input: buy the 30-gem emote. Expected: 70 gems and the emote in the collection
Precondition: 100 gems. Input: buy the 30-gem emote. Expected: 130 gems and the emote in the collection
Input: buy the 30-gem emote. Expected: the emote in the collection
Precondition: 100 gems. Input: buy the 30-gem emote. Expected: 70 gems, the emote in the collection and a purchase e-mail sent
why: The Given becomes the precondition, the When the input, and the Then the expected postconditions: both of them.

distractorNotes.B: Wrong expected result: buying spends gems.
distractorNotes.C: Drops the precondition and half of the expected result (the balance).
distractorNotes.D: Adds an e-mail that the criterion never mentions: it goes beyond the story.

stem: Story: "As a player, I want to redeem a promo code, so that I get its reward." Acceptance criteria: a valid, unused code grants the reward; a used code shows "Already redeemed"; an expired code shows "Code expired". Which is a NEGATIVE test case derived from these criteria?
options: Enter a valid, unused code and check the reward is granted
Check that redeemed codes can be shared on social media
Enter an expired code and check that "Code expired" is shown and no reward is granted
Check that a redemption completes in under one second
why: An expired code is an error condition from the criteria: a negative test case.

distractorNotes.A: This is the positive test case.
distractorNotes.B: Goes beyond the story; sharing is not mentioned.
distractorNotes.D: A non-functional check, and not one of the criteria.

stem: Acceptance criterion: "A squad name must be 3 to 12 characters long." The team applies 2-value boundary value analysis while deriving ATDD test cases. Which name lengths should the test cases use?
options: 3 and 12
0 and 13
why: Techniques from §4.2 can be used in ATDD. 2-value BVA on 3–12 gives 2, 3, 12 and 13.

distractorNotes.A: One value per partition: that is EP, not BVA.
distractorNotes.B: Only the valid boundary values; the neighbours in the invalid partitions are missing.
distractorNotes.C: Misses 3 and 12, and 0 is not a neighbour of a boundary.

stem: For a "quick match" story, the team has written positive and negative ATDD test cases. The acceptance criteria also say that matchmaking must find a game within 60 seconds in 95% of attempts. What should the team do next?
options: Stop: non-functional characteristics are outside ATDD
Write a test case for the 60-second performance criterion
Add test cases for ranked matches, which the story does not mention
Turn the positive tests into unit tests for each method
why: After positive and negative test cases, ATDD covers the non-functional quality characteristics, here performance efficiency.

distractorNotes.A: ATDD does cover non-functional characteristics, as its final step.
distractorNotes.C: Test cases must not go beyond the story.
distractorNotes.D: Unit tests are not the next step of ATDD; the acceptance tests stay at story level.

stem: A tester writes the ATDD test cases for a story in the format of the team's test automation framework. What does this make possible?
options: Developers can automate them by writing supporting code while implementing the story, so they become executable requirements
The test cases no longer need to be understandable to stakeholders
The specification workshop can be skipped
The test cases can cover features beyond the story
why: Test cases in a framework-supported format can be automated while the feature is built; the acceptance tests then act as executable requirements.

distractorNotes.B: ATDD test cases must stay understandable to stakeholders, whatever the format.
distractorNotes.C: The workshop is still where the story and criteria are clarified.
distractorNotes.D: Test cases must not go beyond the story, automated or not.
